claims.claim: Severian was Bishop of Gabala in Syria.
Severian flourished around 398 AD and was active in Constantinople from around 400 until 404.
Severian died after 408, with some sources giving dates as late as 425.
Severian was a popular preacher in Constantinople who became the enemy of John Chrysostom and helped condemn him at the Synod of the Oak.
Severian was favored by Empress Eudoxia and preached with a distinct Syrian accent.
Severian composed commentaries on Job, though these are now lost.
There are four homilies on Job, and the last three may be by Severian of Gabala.
Severian's works, including his homilies on Job, survive primarily among the spuria attributed to his enemy John Chrysostom.
Severian's depiction of Job as an athlete is part of a broader patristic tradition that used athletic metaphors to frame human suffering and model Christian endurance.
More than 50 of Severian's sermons are extant, though almost none have been critically edited and some remain unpublished.
